open_findings: F-002 / F-019 OPEN, MEASURED, MUST NOT BE TUNED AWAY: false interventions are 91.08% against a 2% target. Broken out by stakes: 0% below Rs.100, 100% above. NOT detector noise -- at Rs.40,000 impact with a 2.5x reversibility multiplier, L0_pass only wins if P(defect) < ~0.0001, and the detector's floor on clean text is ~0.019. 'false interventions <= 2%' and 'impact_inr: 40000 with lambda_time 0.40' cannot both hold. The live question is the IMPACT MODEL: impact_inr is a per-request stake charged in full to every sentence, so a five-sentence answer is charged five times the harm the request can cause. Three defensible resolutions (discount per sentence / raise lambda_time / re-target the metric per stakes band); choosing is a deliberate decision, not a tuning pass. LIVE EVIDENCE 2026-08-26: Scene 1 against the real engine on real Ollama produced L5_block (loss Rs.241.89, runner-up L4_hold) on the sentence 'When prepaying a floating-rate home loan, the applicable charge depends on your loan agreement.' -- a hedged, non-committal, essentially harmless answer. Nothing was delivered to the customer. THIS IS DEMO-BLOCKING: the flagship scene currently blocks a reasonable answer, and it is the same root cause as the 91% false-intervention rate rather than a separate bug. CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-26: a trained observer probe (AUROC 0.945 held-out, +0.11 over the best lexical signal) leaves the clean-text floor essentially unchanged at 0.029. Better ML does not close this. It is a decision about the impact model.

F-019 ANSWERED (not closed -- it needs your decision): my first verdict 'jointly infeasible' was WRONG. Decomposed, the disruptive false-intervention target IS achievable below a ~0.001% detector floor (zero repairs/holds/blocks on clean traffic, 100% catch). The annotation-inclusive target is missed at every floor and the entire residual is L1_annotate on high-stakes answers. So: a stateable ML goal for the observer probe, plus one definitional question about whether adding a citation counts as a false intervention.
rework confidence scaled from zero at the similarity bar, making the bar meaningless -- a match that just cleared it charged nothing. Now has an explicit floor.
fairness extractor flagged a paraphrased approval as bias; decided-vs-unreadable is now extraction_uncertain, not disparity.
judge confidence parser dropped any value with trailing punctuation ('confidence 0.85.'), silently losing every stated confidence.

TRAIN/SERVE SKEW in the observer probe: trained with untrusted passages in the premise, served without them. Cost ~0.07 AUROC (0.907 -> 0.837) and nothing errored -- it would have read as 'the probe is weak'. Training now matches serving; serving is the side that cannot move, because a poisoned document in the premise makes the attacker's own claim genuinely entailed.

observe_deadline_ms was 120 ms, but the observer probe costs ~100 ms and the claim verifier another ~100 -- so the probe could NEVER have run in production, and neither could both signals together. The 120 ms figure treated Lane B as if it were on the critical path; it is not, it runs concurrently with generating the next sentence (1-3 s locally) behind the commit buffer. Raised to 800 ms, which is comfortably under the generator and over both signals. What is actually spent shows up as `gate_hold` in /admin/latency, which is the number to watch rather than the ceiling.

Different seeds gave different triples, so it looked fine, but the calibrator had read every document the eval set was built from. Now partitioned BY DOCUMENT, stratified by domain, zero shared -- and re-measured. ECE unchanged (0.0037), false interventions 91.08% -> 85.35%, and verification cost 3.60% -> 5.20%, which now MISSES its target: the leak had been hiding it.

D-010: calibration is fitted on INDUCED failures, not human labels. It calibrates; it does not audit. D2-B3's hand-labelled 300 remains outstanding and is what the meta-monitor must re-score.

D-011: `make eval` holds generation FIXED across both arms (paired design). This is a methodological choice, not a shortcut -- it attributes every off-vs-on difference to Interlock rather than to sampling noise -- but it means generation latency and billing are modelled rather than observed.

D-012: the plan names DeBERTa-v3-base for the observer. transformers 5.x cannot load its tokenizer -- it misroutes the SentencePiece model to the tiktoken parser, which fails on the binary file, and installing sentencepiece/tiktoken does not help because the routing happens before either is consulted. The encoder is configurable and defaults to an NLI cross-encoder whose tokenizer loads natively; NLI is arguably the better base since grounding IS entailment.
